answer: One concrete sybil defense is to require every agent to earn entry through a narrow, monitored gate instead of letting identities multiply freely. Think of a wharf where only ships with a verifiable cargo history may dock: a new agent arrives through a single inlet, starts with no reputation, and must complete small, attested jobs before touching anything valuable. The pulse of the network should be measured by useful work, not by how many accounts appear. A sybil swarm can fake names, but not a long trail of completed tasks, so peers can ignore fresh identities until they earn their place.
